confirmed.title: setTimeout non-clearé lors de copie crash report
confirmed.why: La fonction _copierCrashReport() lance un setTimeout(1800ms) pour restaurer le texte du bouton. Si la modale est fermée pendant l'exécution du timeout, ce timer continue de s'exécuter et tentera d'accéder à un bouton détaché du DOM. Sans AbortController/clearTimeout, le timeout survit et occupe la mémoire inutilement.
confirmed.fix_hint: Capturer l'id du setTimeout et le clearTimeout en fermer(), ou utiliser un AbortController côté Promise avec timeout abort. Pattern analogue au Pattern A (v1.43.26) pour _afficherCrashDetail().

verdicts.reason: Le setTimeout non-clearé existe réellement ligne 834 (et 887 identique). Aucun AbortController ni mécanisme global de cleanup des timers n'est implémenté. Quand fermer() retire l'élément DOM, le timer continue de s'exécuter jusqu'à expiration. C'est un anti-pattern confirmé, même s'il ne cause pas une fuite critique grâce à la garde 'if (btn)' et au timeout court (1800ms). Le code ne stocke pas les timer IDs pour les nettoyer lors de la fermeture de la modale.

The finding is valid. Code analysis confirms: (1) Line 834 in _copierCrashReport() and line 887 in the main copy button handler both launch setTimeout(1800ms) without tracking the timeout ID. (2) When the modal is closed via fermer() (line 903) or close() (line 815), neither function calls clearTimeout or maintains a registry of active timers. (3) The setTimeout callback captures btn in closure; even if the node is detached from DOM, the callback executes on the orphaned reference after 1800ms, keeping the btn reference and closure variables alive until the timeout fires. (4) The codebase shows v1.43.26 just fixed event listener leaks (lines 808-811, 907-910 comments reference this), but made zero changes to setTimeout cleanup patterns — the bug was not addressed in that patch. (5) While the impact is modest (1.8s micro-leak on a debug-only modal feature), it is a genuine, unmitigated memory leak in the current shipping code.

verdicts.reason: Code static audit confirms the finding is real: 1) Line 887 contains a setTimeout(1800ms) with no clearTimeout in fermer() (lines 903-911), 2) identical pattern to line 834 which is also mentioned as buggy, 3) fermer() only cleans DOM via removeChild (line 906), not pending timeouts, 4) the setTimeout closure retains a reference to 'btn' element even after DOM removal, creating a true race condition if user closes modal within 1.8s of clicking copy. The null-check 'if (btn)' is insufficient - it only prevents the assignment, but the timeout still executes and holds memory. No variable tracking pending timeouts exists in the module scope. This is a legitimate (though low-impact) memory leak affecting interactive responsiveness, not a false positive.

Le finding est valide. Le code à la ligne 887 (et ligne 834) lance un setTimeout sans le tracker ni le nettoyer à la fermeture de la modale.
